messages:
maria: Heads up — customer X is onboarding Private VPC in Nov. They expect a Q4 traffic spike and asked for an on-prem hardware readiness plan. Rough forecast they gave: 600k tokens/hr baseline, 2.4M tokens/hr peak (4x), avg seq len ~120, ~75% text-generation, 25% embeddings. Need GPU mix, headroom, power/cooling, procurement ETA. cc @jonathan @kevin

jonathan: Quick back-of-envelope: 2.4M tokens/hr -> ~667 tokens/sec. If we assume ~40 tokens/sec sustained per A100-80GB (with batching + KV caching), that's ~17 A100 GPUs. H100 could be ~2–2.5x faster for same config -> ~7–9 H100 GPUs. Important caveats: perf numbers depend on batch size, context length, and whether you can use KV / prefix caching. Also factor tail-latency and canary traffic. My suggested starter configs:

- Conservative (higher headroom): H100 x 12 (reserve 3-4 for canary/failover)
- Cost-optimized: A100 x 20 with aggressive batching and larger batch windows

Also consider model sharding vs single-GPU model (if the model fits 80GB, single-node is simpler).

kevin: +1 on H100 if customer can afford it. A few infra notes:
- NVLink & PCIe topology matters for sharded setups. If you're doing KV streaming or cross-GPU attention, NVLink + correct topology is required.
- Network: for multi-node RDMA/InfiniBand setups plan for 100Gbps per rack. For single-node serving (model fits on GPU), 40–50Gbps NIC often OK.
- Rack constraints: customer only has 2 racks available. If you need H100 density, validate PDU capacity and cooling (see below).

sre_bot: historical-metrics: last year's busiest private customer peaked at 1.9M tokens/hr on an 8x H100 configuration with ~30% batching and KV caching. Incident logs show tail-latency spikes when local NVMe IO > 60% during heavy cache eviction (incidents/2025-11-12).

maria: They require 99.9% SLA and limited rack space (2 racks). Procurement question: ETA for H100s? Also need recommended per-rack power and cooling numbers to include in the customer checklist.

kevin: Procurement lead times (current market): H100 ~10–14 weeks, A100 ~6–8 weeks (can vary by vendor). Power estimates: H100 card ~700–800W at peak compute load. Plan rack power ~12kW under heavy load; design for 15kW+ to include PDUs, fans, switch power, and overhead. Cooling: chilled-water / high-capacity CRAC recommended for >10kW racks. Spare capacity: keep at least 2 GPUs hot-spare + 1 spare node for failover.

jonathan: Sizing formula I use (putting numbers):
```
tokens_per_sec = tokens_per_hour / 3600
tokens_per_gpu = measured_tokens_sec_per_gpu (depends on model, e.g. 40 t/s for A100)
utilization_target = 0.65  # keep headroom for tail latency
required_gpus = ceil(tokens_per_sec / (tokens_per_gpu * utilization_target))
```
Example: tokens_per_sec=667, tokens_per_gpu=40, utilization_target=0.65 -> required_gpus = ceil(667 / (40*0.65)) = 26 (A100) -> H100 at 90 t/s -> ceil(667 / (90*0.65)) = 12. Those are conservative to avoid latency regressions.

maria: Good, that helps. Any advice on quantization/model variants or storage sizing for model artifacts and KV cache? Customer wants to run multiple versions in parallel during rollout.

jonathan: Quantization: if the model supports 4-bit or LLM.int8, you can reduce memory footprint significantly and bump throughput. That may let you fit larger context on fewer GPUs. For embeddings-heavy traffic, consider offloading embedding-only requests to a CPU-backed vector service (saves GPU hours).
Storage sizing: assume ~80–160GB per model (FP16) depending on architecture. Plan for model versions + backups -> 500GB–1TB of persistent model storage per node cluster. Local NVMe for KV/cache: 1TB per node recommended.

kevin: Monitoring & tests to mandate in the runbook:
- Token-level metrics (tokens/sec, per-route)
- GPU memory pressure and utilization
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV) and eviction logs
- NIC error/collisions, disk IO saturation alerts
- Proactive soak test: run 48–72h soak at 1.5x expected peak with synthetic traffic and verify tail latency p99/p999 targets

maria: Awesome. I'll assemble an HW readiness checklist with these numbers and the procurement timeline. I'll also include a recommended acceptance test plan and ask the customer to confirm rack/power. Drafting doc now and will share link. https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pvt-deploy-hw-readiness (internal). :thumbsup:

jonathan: One more note: for cost tuning, we can propose a hybrid approach — reserve baseline capacity on dedicated nodes and allow burst to a hosted region (if customer permits egress) to avoid overprovisioning for rare peaks. If they insist on fully isolated on-prem, lean toward higher headroom + spare pool.

kevin: Also flag procurement & EOL: ask vendor for firmware/driver compatibility window and spare parts SLA. For enterprise customers, warranty on-site replacement is a big win.

maria: Thanks all — will push to customer and reopen thread after their rack/power confirmation.
